sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice C.V.Bhaskar Reddy
 Writ Petition No.8692 of 2013
Order:

This Writ Petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is filed by the petitioners, seeking the following relief:
"...to issue an order writ or direction particularly one in the nature of WRIT OF MANDAMUS deciaring the proceedings of the 2nd Respondent bearing No G3/2755/12 dated 19 06 2012 in refusing to admit the application of the Petitioners for enhancement of compensation over the lands acquired for widening of National Highway Road No.7 applying Article 137 of Limitation Act, 1963 calculating from the date of award as arbitrary illegal unjust and unconstitutional and in violation of principles of natural justice and Limitation Act, 1963 N H Act 1956
consequently call for the records and set aside the proceedings bearing No G3/2755/12 dated 19 06 2012 and direct the 2nd Respondent to arbitrate for enhancement and pass..."
2. It is stated that the petitioners are the absolute owners and pattadars of the land forming part of various survey numbers in Thimmapur Village, Itikyal Mandal, Mahaboobnagar District.

The case of the petitioners is that their lands were acquired by the respondents by issuing notification under the provisions of the National Highways Act, 1956 (for short, "the Act") for the purpose of expansion of National Highway No.7.

It is the further case of the petitioners that respondent No.3 also passed an award vide 2 CVBR,J wp_8692_2013 proceedings No.G1/4925/2006, dated 11.06.2007,
determining the market value at Rs.2,00,000/- per acre.
Aggrieved by the said award, the petitioners filed the applications, dated 13.08.2010 and 09.08.2011, under Section 3G (5) of the Act before respondent No.2, seeking enhancement of the compensation.

The grievance of the petitioners is that the said applications were rejected by respondent No.2 vide impugned proceedings, dated 19.06.2012 on the ground that there was delay in filing such applications.

3. Smt. N. Shoba, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners contended that Section 3G (5) of the Act does not prescribe any time limitation and therefore, the respondents are having the power to entertain the applications while exercising the powers under Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963.

Learned counsel further submitted that the issue raised in this writ petition is squarely covered by the order of this Court in W.P.No.7815 of 2010 dated 28.02.2011, wherein this Court has held as under:
"Section 3 G (5) of the Act does not stipulate any time within which the application for reference must be 3 CVBR,J wp_8692_2013 made.
The claims made by the owners of the neighbouring lands are under the consideration by the time the petitioner submitted the reminder on 10.08.2009.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners therefore prayed this Court to extend similar relief to the petitioners herein on par with the petitioner in W.P.No.7815 of 2010.
5. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing for respondent Nos.2 and 3 has not disputed the said fact.

6. Therefore, in terms of the orders passed by this Court in W.P.No.7815 of 2010 dated 28.02.2011,
this Writ Petition is allowed and the impugned proceedings bearing No.G3/2755/12, dated 19.06.2012 issued by respondent No.2 are hereby set aside.

Respondent No.2 is directed to consider the applications, dated 13.08.2010 and 09.08.2011 submitted by the petitioners under Section 3G (5) of the Act and pass appropriate orders, duly taking into account the orders passed by him for the lands of the similarly situated 4 CVBR,J wp_8692_2013 persons i.e., petitioner in W.P.No.7815 of 2010, which are acquired under the same notification, within a period of three (03) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
